assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos (2013) and the 2017 association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 opened a new window on the universe. This is a discovery made by nature giving us a clue, which is what I look for. It also bears on the origin of cosmic rays and on the physics of the most extreme accelerators.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and drove IceCube, and Karle has been a central experimental leader of the collaboration. A two-person prize looks coherent, though a large collaboration and the earlier pioneers of the concept (e.g. other detector pioneers) complicate the story, and I cannot verify the exact internal credit.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation of the diffuse flux, plus the Galactic-plane neutrino map and NGC 1068 evidence, make the discovery robust. The field is mature enough for recognition, and the Nobel committee has recognised neutrino astronomy only partly (Koshiba, Davis) in the past.
uncertainties: Source identification is still incomplete; only TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 are individually significant.
Credit among IceCube leadership and predecessors such as DUMAND/Baikal/ANTARES is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators are a conceptually new phase of matter with experimental realisation: Kane-Mele theory, the HgTe quantum spin Hall effect observed by the Molenkamp group, and 3D topological insulators observed by ARPES. The discovery has a clear structure, lasting impact across condensed matter and strong links to the already-recognised topological phases.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the theory, Molenkamp (with the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal) the first experimental realisation, and Hasan the first 3D topological insulator observation. The three-person limit forces leaving out Eugene Mele, and Bernevig, Zhang and others are not even on the credited list, so allocation is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups over fifteen years, with stable interpretation. Recognition is timely, even somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Omitting Eugene J. Mele, who co-authored the key Kane-Mele papers, is a real fairness issue.
The relative priority of the HgTe theory proposal versus the experiment and of Bi-Sb/Bi2Se3 work is a matter of dispute.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on the magic-wavelength idea, has taken timekeeping to the 10^-18 level and opens routes to tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a redefinition of the second. It is a clean, precisely defined invention with a measurable impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first clocks; Jun Ye brought them to extraordinary accuracy and used them for many-body and gravitational-redshift measurements. A fair two-person configuration, though Hall and Hansch (2005 prize) and ion-clock work by Wineland and others are part of the backdrop.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs reproduce and compare the clocks. The technology is mature; the redefinition of the SI second is still pending, which could argue for either waiting or recognising now.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier Nobel for the frequency comb and Wineland's ion clocks may be seen as incremental.
Whether Ye's contribution is better described as clock engineering or as a distinct discovery is arguable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP mapped the cosmic microwave background with high precision and pinned down the parameters of the standard cosmological model: age, geometry, matter and dark-energy content, reionisation. As a physicist who thinks about dark energy, I regard this as the observational foundation that every theorist must reckon with.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Spergel led the cosmological parameter analysis, and Page was a leading instrument scientist. The mission was a large team, and the Wilkinson-era leadership (e.g. David Wilkinson, deceased) and Planck complicate credit, but this trio is defensible.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed and superseded in precision by Planck; the interpretation is very stable. It may seem late, but the 2006 and 2019 prizes covered CMB anisotropy and cosmology partially, which weighs against it.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2006 COBE prize and the 2019 cosmology prize may make the committee judge WMAP as an increment.
Credit within a large collaboration is hard to apportion with only three names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED reached strong coupling of microwave photons and superconducting artificial atoms on a chip, and it is the architecture underlying present superconducting quantum processors. The discovery is original and both conceptual and technological.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf wrote the theory proposal (2004) and the first experiment (Wallraff et al. 2004). Three names is plausible, but Girvin and Devoret's group are left out, and the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits already recognised related ground.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed and widely adopted. The 2025 prize reduces the room for a closely related award in the near term.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recent 2025 prize for superconducting circuits may count against it.
Selection among Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf, Wallraff, Devoret is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum computing with trapped ions and its experimental realisation, including entangling gates and teleportation, made quantum information processing a laboratory reality. It is a significant advance in both fundamental physics and technology.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the 1995 proposal; Blatt led key experiments (the Innsbruck group), while Wineland and his NIST group did the first gate demonstration and shared the 2012 prize. That makes the credit less clean than I would like.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many labs, with a commercial platform emerging. Timing is acceptable, but Wineland's 2012 prize and the more recent 2025 prize on quantum circuits reduce novelty.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 Wineland-Haroche prize and with the cold atom and Rydberg candidates.
Relationship with B047 on the same names suggests the committee must decide how to frame it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* (2019) and Sgr A* (2022) directly show the shadow of black holes, consistent with general relativity. This is nature giving a clue about strong-field gravity, and the existential appeal of seeing a black hole appeals to me. The impact is clear and communicable.
assessment.attribution: Doeleman directed the EHT project and Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, but the result is a collaboration of hundreds, so a fair prize configuration is hard. James M. Moran is credited as well, and the key credit (e.g. VLBI technique developers) is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Two independent targets are imaged, but the images rest on elaborate calibration and imaging methods, and the physical interpretation (e.g. tests of GR, spin) is still developing. It is probably early and the 2020 prize already honoured black holes.
uncertainties: Collaboration scale makes attribution to two or three people difficult.
Interpretive stability and the precision of GR tests are still evolving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing arrays have found evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background (2023), most plausibly from supermassive black-hole binaries. This is a new window on gravitational waves and a direct observational clue about galaxy evolution and perhaps new physics.
assessment.attribution: The pulsar timing array efforts (EPTA, NANOGrav, PPTA) are collaborations. Kramer, McLaughlin and Manchester represent the three pillars, but the credit is arguably diffuse and I cannot verify who the decisive individuals are.
assessment.maturity: The evidence is at about 3-4 sigma for Hellings-Downs correlation and not yet a 5 sigma detection; the origin is not settled. This makes it premature, which is why it sits last on my ballot.
uncertainties: The detection significance is below discovery level; confirmation by combined IPTA data is pending.
The source (astrophysical versus cosmological) is not established.
Attribution across three large collaborations is unclear.
